title: Shell execution probes report granted based only on runtime availability
reasoning: `probeShellExecution` treats `verifyShellExecutionCapability` success as a granted permission, but the verifier only checks that PowerShell, `osascript`, bash, or sh is available. That means `checkPermissions` can mark `shell_execution` granted on ordinary systems even if the user has never completed the shell-execution authorization flow. The request path runs an elevated authentication prompt, but that result is not persisted and is not what subsequent probes check.
reproduction: On macOS, Windows, or Linux with a normal shell runtime installed, run the shell execution probe before any explicit grant; it will return `granted` when the runtime command exists.
recommendation: Separate runtime capability from permission grant state. Persist a successful explicit shell-execution grant, and have `probeShellExecution` require that stored grant plus runtime availability before returning `granted`.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for pre-grant shell execution status or the difference between runtime availability and permission authorization.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test where shell runtime verification succeeds but no stored shell permission exists, and assert `probeShellExecution` returns `needs-action`; then assert a successful request stores a grant and later probes can return granted.
minimumFixScope: Update shell execution probe/request state handling and add focused permission-state tests.
